headline: This law updates the African Growth and Opportunity Act and the Millennium Challenge Act, mostly by urging federal agencies to expand trade help and by changing rules for aid compacts.
what_it_does: The law directs the President to set up a website with information about the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA). It urges the government to promote AGOA trade benefits, help African businesses with training and quality standards, and support trade among eligible sub-Saharan African countries. It also changes the Millennium Challenge Act of 2003 so an eligible country with a compact can enter one additional concurrent compact under set conditions, and it sets new criteria for certain candidate countries beginning in fiscal year 2013.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses and entrepreneurs in eligible sub-Saharan African countries
who_it_affects.how: They may get training, capacity-building help, and easier access to information about AGOA trade benefits.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. importers and traders who use AGOA trade benefits
who_it_affects.how: They can find AGOA information in one place on a government website that the law requires.

who_it_affects.group: Governments of eligible sub-Saharan African countries
who_it_affects.how: They may be able to enter an additional Millennium Challenge compact and must meet new performance and eligibility criteria.

who_it_affects.group: Millennium Challenge Corporation and its Board of Directors
who_it_affects.how: They must provide the Board with information on a candidate country's treatment of civil society and assess sub-national partnerships.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted April 23, 2018; the new Millennium Challenge criteria begin with fiscal year 2013, and many provisions are urged rather than required.
